title: String List Codec
statement:
Design a reversible text format: turn a list of strings into one string, and recover the list from that string.

Contract
- `encode(strings)` accepts a non-null list whose entries are non-null strings. Entries may be
  empty and may contain any characters, including commas, quotes, digits, `#`, newlines,
  and non-ASCII text. The list itself may be empty.
- `encode` returns a non-null string. The exact format is yours to choose.
- `decode(encoded)` receives only strings produced by your own `encode` and must return a list
  equal to the original (same size, same order, same contents). Do not mutate the input list.
- The two methods share no state between calls.

Examples
- Decoding the encoding of `["hello", "world"]` returns `["hello", "world"]`.
- Decoding the encoding of `[""]` returns a list with one empty string, which differs from an empty list.
- Decoding the encoding of `["a,b", "c"]` returns `["a,b", "c"]`; separators inside entries cause no confusion.
hints: A plain separator character fails because the entries themselves may contain it, and an empty list must differ from a list with one empty string.
Either escape the separator inside entries, or write each entry's length before its text so the decoder knows exactly how many characters to take.

With length prefixes, read digits up to a marker, then take that many characters and move on. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for both methods, where n is the total number of characters across all entries.
inputSyntax: Input: the strings joined by | inside square brackets, for example: [hello||a,b|w#rld]
